claims.text: Data center revenue is still growing year over year.
queries: Data Center revenue increase compared to prior year
claims.rationale: Two consecutive quarters show Data Center revenue up from a year earlier, so the claim holds as of the latest reported period. The risk-factor language is context on future volatility, not evidence against current growth.

claims.text: A small number of customers account for a large share of revenue.
queries: loss of a key customer risk
claims.rationale: Every period disclosed shows individual direct customers at double-digit shares of revenue, and the company describes revenue as concentrated, so the claim is well supported.

claims.text: Export controls on sales to China are restricting revenue.
claims.rationale: The passages show export controls had a real, quantified effect through the H20 charge and have limited licensed China sales to small amounts. They do not show the size of the restriction on revenue, and company-wide revenue is growing strongly, so the claim holds in direction but its materiality is unclear.

The evidence is mixed and depends on the comparison period. Year over year, gross margin is higher in fiscal 2027 quarters, but much of that is recovery from the depressed fiscal 2026 base. Sequentially it is approximately flat at about 75%, and the last full fiscal year showed a decline. The claim of expansion is supported only for the year-over-year view and is not supported as an ongoing upward trend.

claims.text: The company depends on a limited number of suppliers to manufacture its products.
claims.rationale: The risk factors state that the number of suppliers is limited and that manufacturing is fully outsourced, so the claim is supported. The business description points to efforts to diversify, which tempers it somewhat.

brief.summary: Data Center revenue is still growing year over year (Supported): $89.0 billion, up 117%, in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027. Customer concentration is Supported: three direct customers represented 16%, 15% and 13% of first-half revenue. Export controls restricting revenue is Mixed evidence: a $4.5 billion H20 charge, yet quarterly revenue was $96.22B, up 105.9%. Gross margin expansion is Mixed evidence: sequentially flat at 75.0%, and fiscal 2026 fell to 71.1% from 75.0%. Supplier dependence is Mixed evidence: concentration risk is disclosed, partly offset by expanded supplier relationships. For the overweight decision, growth and concentration are the firmest points.
unknowns: Whether Data Center growth will continue in the quarter due next is not answered by the passages.
The passages do not give the expected figures or guidance for the next report.
The identities of the customers are not given in these passages.
Indirect customer shares are estimates and are not quantified in these passages.
Whether the direct customers are separate end buyers or resell to the same end users is not stated.
How much revenue China represented before the controls, and what it is now.
Whether H200 shipments to China will be allowed and generate revenue.
How much of the restriction affects current-quarter revenue rather than past inventory charges.
The effect of the expected government share of licensed sales and of the tariff on H200 imports on future revenue and margins.
Whether future changes to export controls will tighten or loosen restrictions.
Whether gross margin will rise, hold or fall in the next quarter, which is what matters for the earnings decision.
How much of the margin level depends on Blackwell Ultra mix and whether that mix can improve further.
next_steps: Test whether Data Center growth can persist given the warned volatility from faster product transitions.
Assess how the largest direct customers' share of revenue could affect results if one reduces orders.
Check whether export controls are reducing demand outside China, such as Europe, Latin America and Southeast Asia.
Examine what drives gross margin beyond the H20 charge and Blackwell Ultra mix.

items.title: Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers
items.locator: Item 5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers
opening: On November 11, 2026, the Board of Directors, or the Board, of NVIDIA Corporation accepted the resignation of Jen-Hsun Huang, as NVIDIA’s President, Chief Executive Officer and member of the Board, effective immediately.

Following Mr. Huang’s resignation, the Board appointed NVIDIA’s Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette M. Kress, age 59, to serve as interim Chief Executive Officer, while the Board conducts a search for a new Chief Executive Officer.

items.title: Other Events
opening: On September 2, 2026, NVIDIA Corporation (“NVIDIA”) entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Hugging Face, Inc. (“Hugging Face”).
Hugging Face operates a platform and community for developing, sharing and deploying open-source models, datasets and applications.

items.title: Results of Operations and Financial Condition
Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement
items.locator: Item 1.01. Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement
opening: On August 17, 2026, NVIDIA Corporation (“NVIDIA”) announced a multi-year partnership with SB Energy Corp. (collectively with its affiliates, “SB Energy”) to advance the development of the PORTS Technology Campus, a large-scale AI data center campus in Pike County, Ohio (the “Portsmouth Site”).
Through the partnership and the credit support described below, NVIDIA has secured land, power, and shell capacity at the Portsmouth Site to host NVIDIA AI compute infrastructure.

opening: The information set forth in Item 1.01 above is hereby incorporated by reference into this Item 2.03.

items.title: Regulation FD Disclosure
opening: On August 17, 2026, NVIDIA issued a press release announcing the partnership with SB Energy.
The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 hereto and is incorporated herein by reference.

items.title: Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers
items.locator: Item 5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers
opening: On June 28, 2026, Ajay K. Puri, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Field Operations of NVIDIA Corporation, or the Company, notified the Company of his intention to retire from his role effective upon the employment commencement date of his successor.
Mr. Puri, a 21-year executive at NVIDIA, is expected to remain with the Company in a senior advisory role to ensure a seamless transition to his successor.

opening: On May 7, 2026, the Board of Directors, or the Board, of NVIDIA Corporation appointed Suzanne Nora Johnson as a member of the Board and as a member of the Audit Committee of the Board and the number of directors constituting the full Board was increased from ten to eleven, in each case effective July 13, 2026.
Ms. Nora Johnson will join the Board effective July 13, 2026, due to a prior professional commitment.

items.locator: Item 5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers
opening: On April 24, 2026, Donald Robertson, Vice President, or VP, and Chief Accounting Officer, or CAO, of NVIDIA Corporation, or the Company, notified the Company of his intention to retire from his role as VP and CAO, effective May 4, 2026.
Following such date, he will remain with the Company as VP, Finance to support various projects until July 1, 2026.

opening: On March 2, 2026, the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors, or the Board, of NVIDIA Corporation, or the Company, adopted the Variable Compensation Plan for Fiscal Year 2027, or the 2027 Plan, which provides eligible executive officers the opportunity to earn a variable cash payment based on the level of achievement by the Company of certain corporate performance goals, or the Performance Goals, during fiscal year 2027.
The Company operates on a fiscal year ending on the last Sunday in January and designates its fiscal year by the year in which that fiscal year ends.
